title: Modular Onramp & Tiering — PRD Sandbox
body:
Context / goal:
This is a scratchpad for a lightweight, modular onboarding + tiering system that helps product engineers pick sensible defaults for cost/latency/fidelity when they first wire Redwood into their app. Aim: reduce time-to-value, reduce support friction, and surface easy upgrade paths to Dedicated/Private without forcing one-size-fits-all defaults.

High-level idea: modular onramp composed of three independent decisions that create a user 'lane' (defaults that can be tuned later):
  1) Fidelity profile (High / Balanced / Frugal) — controls model family, temperature, and max tokens budget
  2) Cost envelope (Pay-as-you-go / Budgeted burst / Committed baseline) — affects batching, caching aggressive-ness, prefetch settings
  3) Resilience lane (Best-effort / SLA-aware / Enterprise-fallbacks) — routing preferences, cross-region fallbacks, canary policy

Why modular?
  - Many customers know only "I want cheap" or "I want fast". Rather than forcing a single default, we let them pick three knobs and map to recommended runtime profiles.
  - Each knob can be surfaced progressively in UI or via API (quickstart = choose 1 of 3 personas, advanced = tune all)
  - Keeps the onboarding flow under 2 minutes for simple signups while still capturing signals for later telemetry and automated recommendations.

User stories (dev persona):
  - As a product engineer I want a 1-click starter that gives reasonable latency and cost so I can demo features quickly.
  - As an ML infra engineer I want explicit, exported defaults for batching/quantization so I can reproduce economics in staging.
  - As a security/compliance lead I want to flag that production traffic must route to Dedicated/Private once a threshold is hit.

Acceptance criteria (minimal MVP):
  - Starter quickstart choice (3 personas) created and applied to a newly-provisioned API key.
  - The system writes a non-destructive runtime profile object attached to the customer metadata (readable via console and API).
  - Telemetry hooks record persona choice + subsequent changes for 90 days.
  - Console shows a clear CTA: "Upgrade to Dedicated if > X RPS or Y monthly token cost" with links to pricing/FAQ.

Proposed data model (notes to self):
  - runtime_profile: string id (e.g., rp-frugal-v1)
  - profile_rules: list of short predicates -> runtime knobs (batch_size_target, quantize_hint, prefix_cache: on/off, model_family_hint)
  - onboarding_event: {persona, chosen_at, modified_at, source} (store as flattened fields in customer meta)

Console UX sketch (short):
  - Step 1: "Pick a starter" (cards: Rapid Demo — Balanced; Low-cost — Frugal; Production-ready — High)
  - Step 2 (optional): advanced toggle expands 3 sliders (latency vs cost, strict fallback vs best-effort, token budget)
  - Step 3: show expected monthly cost range (illustrative) and upgrade triggers (auto-suggest dedicated)

API shape ideas:
  - POST /v1/onramp_profiles {initial_persona: "frugal"} -> returns profile_id, applied_to_api_key
  - GET /v1/customers/{id}/runtime_profile -> flattened csv-like response for UI
  - PATCH /v1/runtime_profiles/{id} -> allow non-breaking overrides

Telemetry / signals to collect (for later ML recommendations):
  - persona chosen, time-to-first-request, token distribution (seq len hist), peak RPS, error rates, percent of responses hitting prefix cache, changes to profile over time

Open questions / tradeoffs:
  - How opinionated should persona->model mappings be? e.g., map "Frugal" to a quantized variant of a smaller model vs a med-size with strong caching
  - Should the onramp enforce quotas for frugal/paid tiers or just give recommendations? (enforce helps avoid bill shocks but adds friction)
  - Integration with Dedicated: when should we nudge vs block? threshold signals vs manual request?
  - Multi-team customers: per-project vs per-org defaults?

Dependencies / infra notes:
  - Need a small metadata store (customer metadata table) + feature flag for rollout.
  - Must add telemetry dimensions in ingestion pipeline (tag events with runtime_profile id).
  - Console changes: quickstart cards + advanced toggle + cost estimator widget (uses token-sim model)

Experiment ideas (short-term A/B):
  - A: default flow = single "Balanced" choice (control)
  - B: modular cards with explicit persona + projected cost (treatment)
  - Measure: activation rate (first 24h), 7-day retention of API usage, support tickets triggered by billing confusion

Edge cases / guardrails:
  - If a user selects "Frugal" but later pushes very long sequences frequently, show an in-console warning with suggested profile change.
  - For enterprise orgs with dedicated contracts, hide the frugal persona and pre-fill recommended profile with SLA-aware defaults.

Next steps / TODOs:
  - [ ] Sketch wireframes for cards + advanced toggle (ask UX: Naoki)
  - [ ] Product -> align on 3 persona names and canonical mappings (owner: Clara)
  - [ ] Engineering feasibility scoping: metadata table + tagging events (owner: Ravi)
  - [ ] Draft small API PRD (~1 pager) that lists endpoints and backwards-compatible constraints

Notes to self (brain-dump):
  - Keep this intentionally small at launch — the value is in lowering the cognitive load. Too many knobs will kill adoption.
  - We should surface an "economics preview" that approximates monthly spend (range) rather than exact pricing. Pricing accuracy can scare people.
  - Consider a follow-up where onboarding choices are auto-reviewed after 14 days and we suggest optimizations (e.g., change model family, enable prefix cache) with one-click apply.

End of scratchpad.
